deep.reconstruction:
PURPOSE. This page corrects the elliptic elements of Pallas so that they fit four mean-opposition places: no. 3 (1805), no. 4 (1807), no. 5 (1808) and no. 6 (1809). It is a preliminary to the 1810 'Disquisitio de elementis ellipticis Palladis'. The 1809 opposition (Sept 22) was computed on the previous page. Times t are in days from 1803 Jan 0.0, meridian of Seeberg. The page is labelled 'Litt. X'.

DATA. Each row gives t, the heliocentric longitude λ at opposition, the geocentric latitude, log R of the Earth, and a fifth column p:
- t = 1064.471030, λ = 67°20'42.9" (used later as 49.90"), latitude −54°30'54.9", log R = 9.9937332, p = 146.01
- t = 1585.611736, λ = 223°37'27.7", +42°11'25.6", 0.0039862, p = 217.50
- t = 2034.891076, λ = 304°2'59.7", +37°43'53.7", 0.0065917, p = 279.12
- t = 2457.675937, λ = 359°40'4.4", −7°22'10.1", 0.0011160, p = 337.11
The last column is precession in arcseconds since 1803.0, at 0.13717"/day (≈50.1"/yr). This is my identification.

Trial elements (1803): node Ω = 172°28'2.00", i = 34°37'12", perihelion π = 120°57'14.13", φ = 14°9'42.54" (e = sin φ). Auxiliary logs:
- log e = 9.3885653
- −log cos φ = 0.0134034
- −3 log cos φ = 0.0402102

STEP 1 (reduction to the orbit). The node is advanced by precession: Ω_k = Ω + p_k, giving 172°30'28.01", 172°31'39.50", 172°32'41.12", 172°33'39.11". Then form λ−Ω_k = 254°50'21.89", 51°5'48.20", 131°30'18.58", 187°6'25.29".
- Argument of latitude: tan u = tan(λ−Ω)/cos i, with log cos i = 9.9153672 and log tan(λ−Ω) = 0.5671021, 0.0931304, 0.0531127, 9.0958006. Result u = 257°25'47.45", 56°24'41.98", 126°3'44.45", 188°36'54.74".
- Side calculation of heliocentric latitude: tan β = tan i·sin(λ−Ω), with log tan i = 9.8390813. Result β = 33°40'37.85", 28°14'48.90", 27°20'22.65", 4°52'55.37" (magnitudes).
- True anomaly: v = u − (π−Ω), with π−Ω = 308°29'12.13". Result v = 308°56'35.32", 107°55'29.85", 177°34'32.32", 240°7'42.61".

STEP 2 (eccentric and mean anomaly).
- Compute log cos v, e cos v (0.1537818, −0.0752967, −0.24444, −0.12185) and log(1+e cos v) (0.0621237, 9.9660011, 9.8782676, 9.9435662).
- Then use sin ½(v−E) = sin ½φ · sin v /√(1+e cos v), with log sin ½φ = 9.0908602. This gives v−E = −10°14'30.85", +14°0'49.5", +0°41'14.73", −13°5'59.80".
- Hence E = 319°11'6.17", 93°54'49.32", 176°53'17.59", 253°13'42.48". The value 176°53'17.59" is repeated at the head of the page.
- Check: log sin E = log sin v − log(1+e cos v) + log cos φ (rows 9.8287276 → 9.8153241, and so on).
- With log e″ = 4.7029904, e sin E = 32984.85", 50347.35", 2739.45", 48318.38".
- M = E − e sin E = 328°20'51.02", 79°55'40.97", 176°7'38.14", 266°39'0.79".

STEP 3 (differential coefficients).
- For π → π + x: dM = −(dM/dv)·x, where dM/dv = cos³φ/(1+e cos v)² (row 9.9597898 − 2 log(1+e cos v)). Coefficients: −0.6847663, −1.0660796, −1.5968151, −1.1821087.
- For φ → φ + y: dM = −sin v (2+e cos v) cos²φ/(1+e cos v)² · y. Coefficients: +1.1830386, −2.0134684, −0.1222974, +1.9855520.

STEP 4 (equations for mean motion). Δt = 521.140706, 449.279340, 422.784861. ΔM = 111°34'49.95" = 401689.95", 96°11'57.17" = 346317.17", 90°31'22.65" = 325882.65".
- Subtracting 770·Δt, Gauss writes RHS 411.606, 371.908, 337.657.
- Coefficient differences: x: −0.3813133, −0.5307355, +0.4147064; y: −3.1965070, +1.8911710, +2.1078494.
- Dividing by Δt, the sidereal motion is n = 770 + 0.7898175 − 0.00073167x − 0.0061337y = 770 + 0.8277879 − 0.0011813x + 0.0042093y = 770 + 0.7986496 + 0.00098089x + 0.0049856y.
- Differences ×1000: 37.9704 − 0.4496332x + 10.3430106y = 0 and −29.1383 + 2.1621953x + 0.776289y = 0.
- Normalised: 3.671115 − 0.0434722x + y = 0 and −37.535380 + 2.785297x + y = 0.
- Subtracting: −41.206495 + 2.82876916x = 0, so x = +14.57", y = −3.04".
- New elements: π = 120°57'28.70", φ = 14°9'39.50".

STEP 5 (mean longitudes, epoch, a).
- Corrected M: 328°20'51.02" − 9.975 − 3.680 → 328°20'37.56", and 266°39'0.79" − 17.2197 − 6.0361 → 266°38'37.53".
- Add π + precession (120°59'54.74", 121°3'5.81") to get mean longitudes L1 = 89°20'32.27" and L6 = 27°41'43.34".
- Sidereal motion n_sid = 770.79829" (it equals ΔM_corrected(6−1)/1393.204907). Tropical motion n_trop = n_sid + 0.13717 = 770.93546"/day.
- Mean-longitude epochs: 1803.0 → 221°23'13.81", 1804.0 (t = 366) → 299°45'56.19".
- Checks:
  - t = 1064 gives 89°14'29.14"; the difference of 6'3.13" = 0.471030·n.
  - t = 2458 gives 27°45'53.17"; the difference of +4'9.83" = 0.324063·n.
  - So both oppositions are represented exactly.
- New logs: log e = 9.3885399, −log cos φ = 0.0134019.
- Kepler III with Gauss's constant: log k″ = 3.5500066; log a^{3/2} = 3.5500066 − 2.8869407 = 0.6630659; log a = 0.4420439 (a ≈ 2.767 AU).
- These elements are continued on the next page (mean longitudes 1802–1811, opposition 1811).
errors: The constant terms of the 2nd and 3rd mean-motion equations do not match the listed ΔM. 346317.17 − 770×449.279340 = 372.078, not 371.908 (diff 0.170"); 325882.65 − 770×422.784861 = 338.307, not 337.657 (diff 0.650"). The first, 411.606, is correct. Using the correct values the system gives x ≈ +14.05", y ≈ −3.10" instead of +14.57", −3.04". The resulting change in elements is about 0.5", so the effect is small, but the solved system is internally inconsistent.

Consistent with the above: the n implied by Gauss's three equations at x = 14.57, y = −3.04 is ≈770.79779". The n he adopts, 770.79829", equals the directly corrected (M6−M1)/Δt. He apparently took n from the end oppositions, not from the solved system.

Column 1 bottom: 328°20'51.02" − 9.975" − 3.680" = 328°20'37.365", but 37.56" is written. Also 1.1830386×3.04 = 3.596, not 3.680, so the y-correction of opposition 3 is not reproduced. Discrepancy ≈0.1–0.2"; it may be a reading problem with the overwritten digits.

Column 2: E − e sin E = 93°54'49.32" − 13°59'7.35" = 79°55'41.97", not 79°55'40.97" as written. The E digits are heavily overwritten, so the written E may be 93°54'48.32". Not resolvable from the transcription.

results.what: Reduction of opposition longitude to argument of latitude, true anomaly and heliocentric latitude: tan u = tan(λ−Ω)/cos i and tan β = tan i sin(λ−Ω)
Eccentric anomaly from true anomaly via sin ½(v−E) = √(r/p) sin ½φ sin v, then Kepler's equation M = E − e sin E
results.usually_credited_to: Gauss (Theoria Motus 1809) for this particular form

results.what: Differential correction of perihelion, φ and mean motion from four oppositions: dM/dπ = −cos³φ/(1+e cos v)², dM/dφ = −sin v(2+e cos v)cos²φ/(1+e cos v)²; elimination of the epoch by differences and exact solution of the 3×2 system
results.modern_name: differential correction of orbital elements (linearised orbit improvement)

results.what: Semi-major axis from mean motion with Gauss's constant k = 3548.1876" (log 3.5500066): log a = (2/3)(log k − log n)
results.modern_name: Kepler's third law with Gaussian gravitational constant

deep.surprise_reason: This is routine working material for Gauss's well-documented Pallas orbit determination of 1809–1810. All methods are his published Theoria Motus techniques. Interest is only archival: it shows the intermediate elements from oppositions 3–6, and two small arithmetic inconsistencies.
transcription_corrections: '0,0128896' (log sin v − log(1+e cos v), col. 2) should be ≈0.0123896.
In the heading, the crossed-out word before 'der Pallas' is a false start; the subject is the elements, not an opposition.
'Ω' next to 0,0134019 is a mark for −log cos φ, not the node.
